question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s dominance within the Chinese Communist Party and People’s Liberation Army drives the near-certain trader consensus that he will remain general secretary through the end of 2026. Extensive purges of senior military and civilian officials, including recent investigations into Central Military Commission members, have eliminated potential rivals while reinforcing loyalty networks rather than signaling weakness. No institutional mechanisms or visible elite factions exist to force an early exit before the 21st Party Congress in late 2027, where Xi is positioned to pursue a fourth term after abolishing presidential term limits. He continues to appear publicly at major events and summits at age 73, with succession planning deferred. Low-probability shifts could still arise from an unforeseen health crisis, elite backlash amid economic pressures, or abrupt diplomatic reversals that fracture internal support.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains wide open more than two years before primaries, with no formal declarations and a crowded field of governors, senators, and House members generating early buzz through fundraising, travel, and polling. Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects this uncertainty, pricing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez narrowly ahead amid her rising support in early-state surveys like New Hampshire and momentum among progressive voters, while Jon Ossoff and Gavin Newsom trail closely on name recognition and positioning. Kamala Harris leads some national polls but trails in markets, highlighting divides between traditional polling and skin-in-the-game pricing. The tight spread among top contenders stems from post-2024 party dynamics, upcoming 2026 midterms as a key test, and unresolved questions over ideological direction and candidate viability. Developments such as midterm results, Senate confirmation fights, or early endorsements could quickly widen gaps.
